Intermittent graceful fallback after canary weight increase due to slow pin handshake

Issue summary:
BrightWrite reports intermittent routing to a degraded fallback model immediately after a canary weight increase for a tenant-pinned variant. Impact is visible for a subset of streaming requests (approx 2-4% of requests during bursts) where responses are truncated or have reduced quality.

Impact:
- Customer-visible reduced generation quality and shorter responses for some streaming sessions.
- Occurs shortly after canary weight adjustments or prewarm churn.
- Requests show a short-lived diversion to a fallback model which is explicitly configured as a safety variant.

Timeline / Observed behavior (customer report):
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Customer increased canary weight from 5% to 25% for route /v1/generate with model redwood-open-13b-v2 and pinned sessions.
- 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC: ~2-4% of streaming sessions returned responses that matched fallback quality signature (shorter completions, truncated tokens).
- 2026-03-10 09:18 UTC: Customer opened support chat referencing request IDs and a short snippet of logs.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Tenant with active pinned sessions to redwood-open-13b-v2.
2) Increase canary weight rapidly (e.g., 5% -> 25%) or trigger prewarm across a shard.
3) Drive sustained concurrent streaming requests (50-200 concurrent streams) with persistent connections/keepalives.
4) Observe ~2-4% of sessions routed to redwood-open-13b-compat-fallback for the first few seconds after the weight change.

Logs & Traces collected:
- Edge request IDs: bw-req-20260310-1123xx (sample set provided by customer).
- Edge logs show handshake timeout events: "pin-handshake: timeout=120ms elapsed=201ms", followed by routing decision "route: fallback-variant chosen by graceful-fallback-policy".
- Orchestrator traces show slow commit latency when writing cohort snapshot to control-plane (commit latency spikes 120-300ms during the window).
- No 5xx from serving runtime; explicit intentional fallback chosen by routing logic.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Roll weight back to prior level (5%) and perform a slower ramp (5% -> 10% -> 15% -> 25% with 2–5 min stabilization).
- If immediate relief required, pin the tenant explicitly to the stable variant on the control plane to avoid canary handshake during traffic.

Initial hypothesis:
- The pin handshake timeout is too aggressive relative to control-plane commit latency under a prewarm/autoscale wave. Sessions that do not receive a timely pin confirmation are routed to the safe fallback. A rapid canary weight change combined with prewarm operations causes transient control-plane commit latency that exceeds handshake window.

Next steps (investigation):
- Correlate orchestrator snapshot commit spikes with edge handshake timeouts (SRE).
- Validate whether handshake timeout values are globally configured or per-route.
- Run a controlled repro in staging mimicking canary weight ramp + concurrent streaming.
- Evaluate increasing handshake window or adding short-lived grace period for pinned sessions during weight ramping.

2026-03-11 16:20 — Engineer (Lina Chen) — Reproduced partial symptom in staging by simulating slow snapshot commit during a weight jump. Observed handshake timeouts and fallback selection. Adding CI repro notes to linked PR.
2026-03-11 18:10 — Support (Evelyn) — Provided customer with temporary ramping guidance and a manual pin option while we validate fix. Customer accepted ramping approach.
2026-03-12 08:55 — SRE (Marco Diaz) — Proposed mitigation: extend handshake window from 150ms -> 300ms and implement short grace window to honor previous pin on in-flight sessions during weight increases. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/7823.
2026-03-12 12:30 — Product Ops (Aaron Blake) — Flagged as potential UX change; will require doc update and canary for config change. Added to rollout checklist.
2026-03-12 14:00 — Support (Evelyn) — Will keep ticket open until control-plane fix is deployed and customer confirms no further fallback occurrences.
- Control-plane snapshot commit latency correlates with prewarm/autoscale spikes.
- Handshake timeout function is conservative (150ms); observed commit latencies up to 300ms under load.
- Fallback routing is working as designed (safety-first) but is surprising to customer because it occurs within seconds of a controlled canary change.
- Staging repro shows same behavior when we inject artificial 200ms commit delay into orchestrator.
- Edge code path does not currently surface a distinct metric for handshake timeouts per-tenant; adding metric suggested.
Work in progress:
- Short-term mitigation: recommended ramping strategy and manual control-plane pin for affected tenant (accepted by customer).
- Medium-term fix: PR #7823 increases handshake timeout and adds 5s grace window for honoring previous pin on in-flight sessions during weight changes.
- Observability actions: add per-tenant handshake timeout metric, alert when handshake-timeouts rate > 0.5% for 5m.
- Post-deploy validation plan: monitor BrightWrite traffic for two hours following rollout and confirm fallback rate falls to baseline (<0.1%).
- Owner for deploy: Marco Diaz (SRE); rollout ETA: 2026-03-15 for canary, full rollout by 2026-03-18 pending canary results.
